 Advertisement Thousands of Mainers are scrambling to find new Medicare coverage amid plan terminations
 As of September, more than 13,111 people were enrolled in nine Medicare Advantage plans that won’t be offered in 2027.
 Advertisement Updated: 6:20 PM EDT Oct 27, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Norah Hogan Chief Investigative Reporter Thousands of Mainers are scrambling to find new Medicare coverage amid plan terminations
 As of September, more than 13,111 people were enrolled in nine Medicare Advantage plans that won’t be offered in 2027.
 Updated: 6:20 PM EDT Oct 27, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Norah Hogan Chief Investigative Reporter WESTBROOK, Maine — Many Maine seniors are scrambling to choose their Medicare coverage after Martin’s Point terminated several Medicare Advantage plans.
 An 8 Investigates analysis of Medicare enrollment data found that five other carriers are also cutting plans, affecting thousands of Mainers. As of September, more than 13,111 people were enrolled in nine Medicare Advantage plans that won’t be offered in 2027. Roughly 31,788 people were enrolled in 11 plans that will no longer over coverage in their county.
 Advertisement “Particularly when your plan is being discontinued, it’s really important that you choose a new plan for next year so that you don’t have any gaps in coverage come January,” said Chloe Gray, volunteer program manager at Age Maine.
 Gray oversees Age Maine’s Medicare counseling program. This year, all of the agency’s one-on-one appointments are booked, and requests for help have nearly doubled. Last October, the agency received roughly 850 calls. As of Monday, it has already received more than 1,500 calls this month.
 “We did see a lot of premiums increase for next year, and some of the extra benefits on plans were reduced,” Gray said. "That’s pretty much across the board that we saw that happening to plans on Medicare Advantage plans and costs going up on prescription drug plans as well for original Medicare."
 Seniors whose plans aren’t being terminated are also feeling the impact of significant changes, including higher premiums, reduced vision, dental and prescription coverage, and changes to provider networks.
 "It seems like almost every year I have to swap plans because the coverages change or the physicians, the primary cares, they come and go,” said John St. Hilaire, who attended a Medicare enrollment counseling session with his wife, Laurie.
 The St. Hilaires sign up for a counseling session every year and usually book their appointment months in advance. John doesn't think they should have to jump through hoops to ensure good coverage, but they're happy for the assistance. 
 "We’re just lucky that people like this, at Age Maine, are there for the people," Laurie said.
 Medicare open enrollment ends Dec. 7, but people enrolled in plans that were terminated will have until the end of the year to choose a new plan. People enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans can also switch plans between January and March, if needed.
 Although counseling sessions are booked, other resources are available, including a comparison tool on the Medicare website, informational videos and a hotline.

 While personal Medicare counseling sessions are booked at aging agencies across the state, many offices offer walk-in-clinics where you can receive assistance in person.
